findings.summary: The class javadoc's account of the bug it exists to fix is factually wrong: it lists three messages under a contains("lease") predicate and says "All three matched", but CommitLog's fence message contains no occurrence of "lease", so that predicate MISSED it -- the opposite failure from the one the paragraph describes.
findings.failure_scenario: CommitLog.fenced (CommitLog.java:530-539) builds exactly "chain sealed at seq 5, continued at epoch 2; this writer is fenced and must stop". Apply the predicate the paragraph names: "...must stop".contains("lease") == false. Only LocalSequencer.java:414 ("lost its lease") and :421 ("released its lease") match, and only one of those two is a fence. Concrete consequence: the implementer of M5.6/M5.6b, for whom this paragraph is the sole written justification, is told the old predicate over-matched, and cannot infer from it how the seal-discovery fence was classified. Verified against the tree: grep for "lease" in *.java matches Belief.java:39 and the two LocalSequencer throws only -- CommitLog's fence string is not among them.
